description: Plain JSON: one terrain letter per 10-mile cell. No archive or decompression needed.
instructions: Each key in rows is an actual signed grid row coordinate, not a sequential row index.
Each row string runs west to east. Character index 0 is column_min. For column c use index c - column_min.
North is positive row; east is positive column. Row entries are ordered north to south for display.
For numeric FPS coordinates X,Y: column=floor(X*12), row=floor(Y*12). Use floor, not truncation, for negatives.
Look up rows[str(row)][column-column_min], then translate the letter with legend. Check bounds first.
A cell spans X=[column/12,(column+1)/12), Y=[row/12,(row+1)/12). Center is ((column+0.5)/12,(row+0.5)/12).
For a named place obtain its FPS coordinates separately; this file contains terrain, not a location-name index.
Use JSON parsing and character indexing for exact lookups; do not count letters visually.
limitations: Approximate dominant terrain only; mixed-terrain percentages, pixel geometry and elevation are omitted.
Boundary cells can contain land and water. Do not use dominant terrain alone for ship navigation.
Edge cells are clipped by the source image, despite the nominal 10-mile cell size.
Compass, legend and scale-bar gaps contain inferred sea. The ranges below identify affected cells, not entirely inferred cells.

inferred_cell_ranges.meaning: Row keys mapped to inclusive [first_column,last_column] ranges containing inferred ocean fill.
